title: Fictional example: protein X and organoid growth

paper.citation: Synthetic teaching example. No published paper or real measurements.
paper.source: Fictional source references below demonstrate the mapping format.
paper.read_scope: Constructed question, three experiments and three observations.

nodes.text: Does protein X contribute to organoid growth?
Protein X contributes to growth in this organoid assay.
nodes.details: The claim is scoped to the tested system and readout.
Perturbation result in the tested cultures; not a claim of direct molecular interaction.

nodes.text: Re-expression of X restores organoid expansion.
nodes.details: The rescue supports specificity within this construct and assay.

nodes.text: X may act through binding to protein Y.
nodes.details: An author's proposed mechanism. Direct binding has not been established.
Human organoids; X knockdown versus non-targeting control; organoid area at 72 h; four independent donor cultures, paired across conditions.
Knockdown plus resistant X versus knockdown plus empty vector, with control cultures; area at 72 h; the same four independent donor cultures.
Co-immunoprecipitation with input and IgG controls plus a positive detection control; assay conditions and sensitivity constrain the negative result.

nodes.text: Knockdown reduces area by 35% at 72 h.
nodes.details: Invented mean relative to paired controls. No uncertainty estimates or p-values were constructed.

nodes.text: Rescue restores area to 95% of control.
nodes.details: Invented mean in the same donor cultures. This is not an independent donor cohort.
A fictional negative assay result. It leaves binding unestablished under the tested conditions.

edges.reason: Answers the starting question within the tested organoid assay.
Compares loss of X with a matched perturbation control.
Tests whether resistant X restores the affected readout.
Examines the proposed binding step under these assay conditions.
Organoid area is the measured readout.
The rescue experiment measures the same readout.
No interaction signal is observed in this assay.
The matched comparison shows reduced expansion after knockdown.
Re-expression restores the measured expansion toward control.
Rescue strengthens the attribution of the growth phenotype to the X perturbation.
Binding remains unestablished; a negative assay does not exclude every interaction condition.

The rescue strengthens specificity in this assay.
The proposed molecular explanation is attached to the central claim without treating it as established evidence.
The proposed growth mechanism presupposes the growth phenotype.
